The CPU tests show that the software behaves as specified. They do not show that a new task will succeed physically or visually; that takes a real run and independent review. Each feature note lists what its component does not guarantee, for example:

 processes running as the same user are not a security boundary;
 the shipped simulator-qualification evaluators cover cloth only, and a task's probe runner is task code;
 the H3 route selects among pre-rendered seeds rather than re-rendering flagged chunks;
 MiniMax-H3's licence restricts using its outputs to train other AI models, so check it for your use. [...] Fail closed. Simulators, models, data and credentials are runtime bindings. A missing binding stops the tool with a message naming it; nothing falls back to a guess. [...] ## Installation

DataFarm needs Linux and Python 3.11 or newer. Media checks use `ffmpeg`, and the sandbox that isolates the expert author uses `bubblewrap`.

```
&& cd'.[dev,workflow]' ' '
```

The core runtime needs only the standard library and Pillow. The `workflow` extra adds the imaging and scientific packages used by the verifiers and dataset tools.

The default H3 renderer needs one GPU with at least 172 GB free per worker.

The repository does not contain simulators, video models, robot assets, data or credentials. Install the components you need (see NOTICE.md) and point DataFarm at them with runtime bindings:

```
$EDITOR# or point DATAFARM_BINDINGS at the file, or set DATAFARM_ ## check prerequisites, no API or GPU calls #
```

results.content:
## Nothing enters the dataset on the agent's word

A generated video can look right and still contradict its labels. Machine checks and an independent reviewer compare every render with its simulated state, and reject failures like these.

### Phantom arm

An arm the simulator does not contain.

Simulator framesimulator

Rejected render with an extra arm render: rejected

### Future state drawn early

The block is in the drawer before the simulator puts it there.

Simulator framesimulator

Rejected render with the block already in the drawer render: rejected

### Invented cloth

A wrist view adds towel where the simulation is empty.

Simulator framesimulator

Rejected render with invented cloth render: rejected [...] Correlation of each view with the simulator video, in frame-difference energy (motion) and image gradients (structure); jumps per 1,000 frames. Means over stack cups, weigh apple, and pull drawer. †Stack cups only; DataFarm on that episode: 0.75, 0.87, 4.2.

The problem

## Robot data is still collected one episode at a time

 Each episode needs a robot, an operator, and a reset.
 Every new task, layout, or scene starts the collection over.
 The cost grows with every episode you record.

DataFarm

## A coding agent takes the teleoperator's place

It does not drive the robot: it compiles the task into a simulation and a render contract, and the farm produces every further episode.

Calibration episode

01Calibrate [...] All cameras in one generation. Head and wrist views are tiled on one canvas and generated as one video, so they share lighting and materials and agree on which objects exist and what each gripper holds.

References and prompts that add no content, and long episodes without drift: references match the simulated task state, prompts describe only the current segment, and long episodes are generated as independent chunks and joined where neighbouring chunks differ least.

| Renderer | Motion ↑ | Structure ↑ | Jumps ↓ |
 ---  --- |
| Direct call, one canvas | 0.07 | 0.16 | 11.2 |
| Direct call, each camera | 0.04 | 0.10 | 8.8 |
| Edge control only | 0.50 | 0.54 | 30.2 |
| DataFarm, each camera† | 0.55 | 0.64 | 40.6 |
| DataFarm | 0.74 | 0.85 | 2.9 |
